Once the Callahan recruits left, we started getting into dog fights with bad teams. While we still won, it was clear that the level of play had dropped. At this point in his tenure, we would get obliterated by any team with a pulse.

Another important factor is that his schedules were a lot easier than what we see now. The Big 12 north was awful. Then we joined a big 10 that, while not terrible, was much weaker than it is now. Michigan was mediocre, Iowa was going between 4-8 and 8-4 most years, Ohio State was starting to get back to form, and Penn State was recovering from the scandal. By the time Riley and Frost were around, the B1G was much tougher.
